premises.text: Aviation must fill a large CO2 gap to reach net-zero by 2050
premises.evidence_span: there's an urgent need to decarbonize aviation

premises.text: Electric aviation must start from light aircraft to fill the emissions gap
premises.evidence_span: we are convinced aviation will be electric. That's a solution to fill this gap. However, we need to start from the light aircraft

premises.text: Hydrogen balances energy efficiency and aircraft range/speed/payload better than batteries or SAF for their jet
premises.evidence_span: hydrogen in the middle has good enough energy efficiency and a good enough aircraft performance

premises.text: An integrated hydrogen-to-propeller powertrain in an aircraft is ready for test flight
premises.evidence_span: an 85 kilowatt powertrain from hydrogen tanks to a propeller

premises.text: Go-to-market is a six-to-eight passenger pressurized business jet matching existing missions via scalable hydrogen architecture
premises.evidence_span: it's a six to eight passengers aircraft pressurized, so you fly in altitude with speed and range of existing aircraft

premises.text: European airports must be ready to supply hydrogen for the jet
premises.evidence_span: we're working with 50 of them to bring hydrogen for our aircraft

value.text: Comparable business-aviation performance without direct emissions
value.evidence_span: we propose comparable performance without the direct emissions

secondary_value.text: Long-run scale to regional and commercial platforms with large CO2 reduction potential
secondary_value.evidence_span: Beyond Aero has a possible CO2 reduction contribution possible of 350 megaton of CO2 equivalent

causal_links.evidence_span: That's what we want to develop at Beyond Aero
fully electric thanks to hydrogen technology
work with European airports for them to be ready for our jet

notes: Battery vs SAF comparison folded into hydrogen choice (P3). Powertrain subsystem cascade folded into P4. LOIs and investor-clients treated as traction. Regional/commercial scale coded as secondary value. Singleton D3 retained: airport hydrogen readiness is separately revisable from the aircraft.
